problem.title: Design a Thread-Safe In-Memory Pub-Sub Message Queue (LLD)
problem.prompt: Implement a thread-safe in-memory Pub-Sub broker supporting `createTopic`, `publish`, `subscribe`, and `resetOffset`—where slow subscribers never block fast subscribers or unrelated topics, and caught-up consumers sleep without busy-waiting.

spark.summary: Design an in-memory Kafka-like Pub-Sub broker supporting multiple topics, concurrent publishers, independent subscriber offsets, and non-spinning `Condition` signaling.
spark.keyTakeaway: When traffic spikes expose hidden coupling, model each `Topic` with an append-only log guarded by a per-topic `ReentrantLock` + `Condition`, and give each `SubscriberWorker` its own `AtomicInteger` offset so slow consumers never block fast ones.
spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** Unlike a point-to-point `BlockingQueue` (where 1 consumer pops and removes each message), Pub-Sub requires every subscriber on a topic to receive all messages independently and support `resetOffset()` for replay—all while isolating slow subscribers and unrelated topics.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts Per-Topic Append Log + Condition Wakeup for Independent Consumers (Publisher -> Topic Log (Lock+Cond) -> Fast Sub (off=42) -> Slow Sub (off=10)); Topic-Isolated Append Log & Per-Subscriber Cursors (Broker Registry -> Topic Append Log -> Fast Worker -> Slow / Replay Worker).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Duplicating messages into `N` separate `BlockingQueue`s wastes `N×` memory and cannot support `resetOffset(0)` replay. This exact in-memory model scales out into distributed streaming logs: **Apache Kafka & Redpanda**: Store immutable per-partition append logs on disk and track per-consumer-group offsets independently for replay.

**Failure Modes & Application:** This exact in-memory model scales out into distributed streaming logs: **Apache Kafka & Redpanda**: Store immutable per-partition append logs on disk and track per-consumer-group offsets independently for replay.

learningJourney.title: Head-of-line blocking, busy-wait CPU burn, and global-lock contention

explanation.foundation: Naive in-memory brokers break in three ways:
explanation.core:
1. **Synchronous Fan-Out**: Calling `subscriber.onMessage(msg)` directly inside `publish()` lets one slow subscriber stall the publisher and all fast subscribers.
2. **Busy-Wait Polling**: `while (offset >= log.size()) {}` burns 100% CPU when caught up.
3. **Global Broker Lock**: Synchronizing all topics on one lock causes `Topic A` traffic to block `Topic B`.

decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: When traffic spikes expose hidden coupling, model each `Topic` with an append-only log guarded by a per-topic `ReentrantLock` + `Condition`, and give each `SubscriberWorker` its own `AtomicInteger` offset so slow consumers never block fast ones.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.

learningJourney.title: Enterprise solution: Per-Topic Log + `Condition` + `AtomicInteger` Offsets

explanation.foundation: Build clean isolation across topics and subscribers:
explanation.core:
- **`ConcurrentHashMap<String, Topic>`**: `createTopic` uses `putIfAbsent` with zero global lock during `publish()`.
- **Per-Topic `ReentrantLock` + `Condition`**: `publish()` appends to `List<Message>` and calls `newMessageCond.signalAll()`. `SubscriberWorker` sleeps via `newMessageCond.await()` inside a `while (offset.get() >= topic.size())` loop (handling spurious wakeups).
- **Independent `AtomicInteger` Offset**: Each `SubscriberWorker` tracks its own offset; `resetOffset(newOffset)` sets the offset and signals the condition variable to replay immediately.
